rfp_requirements.title: File Annual Political Contribution Disclosure with ELEC
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor must file an annual disclosure statement on political contributions with the New Jersey Election Law Enforcement Commission (ELEC) if in a calendar year it receives one or more contracts valued at $50,000.00 or more.

rfp_requirements.title: Allow State research during normal operations
Adhere to State holiday changes
Obtain SCM pre-approval for unscheduled closings
Adhere to Contract Schedule
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor must adhere to the Contract Schedule.

rfp_requirements.title: Provide 24/7 automated response system for non-business hours
rfp_requirements.description: Any automated system used for routine requests during non-business hours must be available 24 hours daily including weekends and holidays.

rfp_requirements.title: Conduct at least six PIF/PFF seminars in different regions
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor must schedule and conduct no less than six PIF/PFF seminars/meetings in different geographic regions during the Implementation Phase.

rfp_requirements.title: Provide comprehensive documentation to SCM per SLA schedule
Any delayed payment plan must be part of PIF/PFF Support Plan
rfp_requirements.description: Any delayed payment schedule beyond the time of installation/activation must be part of the Contractor's proposed PIF/PFF Support Plan.

rfp_requirements.title: Cure membership failure within 10 calendar days
rfp_requirements.description: An Employee who has failed to maintain membership shall be notified and shall have 10 calendar days following receipt of written demand from the Union to cure such failure by tendering the requested dues, or be subject to discharge.

rfp_requirements.title: Adjust schedules for Union meetings and grievance hearings
rfp_requirements.description: The work schedules of Union representatives shall be adjusted to permit attendance at regular Union meetings and grievance hearings provided Employer operations are not unduly impaired.

rfp_requirements.title: Limit Saturday forced overtime to 1 hour
rfp_requirements.description: No Senior Lane Technicians, Lane Technicians, Full and Part-Time Associate Lane Technicians can be forced to work more than 1 hour beyond their scheduled shift on Saturdays.

rfp_requirements.title: Limit Lane Tech compelled overtime to 1 hour
rfp_requirements.description: Senior Lane Technicians, Lane Technicians, Full and Part-Time Associate Lane Technicians cannot be compelled to work more than 1 hour of overtime after their scheduled shift.

rfp_requirements.title: Guarantee 1/2 hour pay for drafted shifts including Saturday
rfp_requirements.description: Employees drafted to work after their scheduled shift, including on Saturday, must be guaranteed one-half hour of overtime pay regardless of time actually worked.

rfp_requirements.title: Grant Union stewards super-seniority for layoff/recall
rfp_requirements.description: Union stewards shall have super-seniority at their assigned station for layoff and recall purposes, provided they are qualified and work the schedule; preference may not displace Employees at other stations.

rfp_requirements.title: Conduct layoffs by location using seniority
rfp_requirements.description: All layoffs must be by location and the selection of employees laid off must be based on bargaining unit seniority, provided remaining employees are willing to work the remaining schedule.

rfp_requirements.title: Allow 7 days to meet on layoff matters
rfp_requirements.description: The Employer must allow seven calendar days from receipt of notification for the Union and affected employees to meet to attempt to resolve layoff matters.

rfp_requirements.title: Allow bumping of junior employees within classification
rfp_requirements.description: Employees scheduled to be laid off in specified classifications must be allowed to displace a junior employee in the same classification from their location/station by seniority; Equipment Repair Technicians are laid off by statewide seniority.

rfp_requirements.title: Part-Time full-time recall contingent on schedule acceptance
rfp_requirements.description: A Part-Time Associate Lane Technician on layoff has recall rights to a full-time position only if willing to work the required full-time schedule.

rfp_requirements.title: Post promotional vacancy notice for 5 working days
rfp_requirements.description: The Employer must post a notice of promotional vacancy on bulletin boards for at least five working days (excluding weekends and holidays) before filling.

rfp_requirements.title: Set Saturday hours for Lane Technicians
rfp_requirements.description: For Saturday, hours of operation for Senior Lane Technicians, Lane Technicians, Full and Part-Time ALTs must not be less than 5 hours or more than 8 hours, subject to State of NJ restrictions.

rfp_requirements.title: Senior Lane Tech makes lunch/break schedules
rfp_requirements.description: All lunch and break schedules are to be made by Senior Lane Technicians for each lane they are responsible for, subject to station management approval (not unreasonably withheld).

rfp_requirements.title: Post workweek schedules one month in advance
rfp_requirements.description: Regular workweek schedules must be posted one month in advance.

rfp_requirements.title: Provide unpaid lunch and paid breaks to Technical/Material/ERT
rfp_requirements.description: Technical Specialists, Material Handler classifications, and Equipment Repair Technicians must receive a one-hour unpaid lunch and four 15-minute paid breaks as schedule permits, without interfering with business or delaying repairs.

rfp_requirements.title: Allow use of accrued vacation for emergency/personal reasons after sick exhausted
rfp_requirements.description: If an Employee has exhausted sick time during a calendar year without using the maximum emergency/personal allowance, the Employee may use accrued and unused vacation time for this purpose until the maximum is reached.

rfp_requirements.title: Grant paid jury duty leave less stipend
rfp_requirements.description: Employees required to serve jury duty during a scheduled workday shall be excused with pay, less the jury stipend, for any calendar day jury duty is performed.

rfp_requirements.title: Grant paid emergency civilian duty leave
rfp_requirements.description: Employees required to perform emergency civilian duty related to national defense or emergency shall be excused with pay up to a maximum of 5 days per calendar year.

rfp_requirements.title: Accrue vacation at beginning of calendar year
rfp_requirements.description: Vacation time accrues at beginning of calendar year in anticipation of continued employment; only one year of vacation credits may be carried forward into the following calendar year.

rfp_requirements.title: Grant additional vacation allowance in year of service change
rfp_requirements.description: If vacation allowance changes based on years of service during any calendar year, the additional annual allowance will be given for that calendar year.

rfp_requirements.title: Use carried-over vacation in following year
rfp_requirements.description: Vacation time carried over into next calendar year must be used in that calendar year.

rfp_requirements.title: Present Step 2 Grievance Within 10 Calendar Days
rfp_requirements.description: If unsettled, the grievance may be presented in Step 2 within 10 calendar days after receipt of the Step 1 answer.

The hearing examiner will prepare a cover letter that includes the date, time, and location of the hearing; the phone

Expedited Hearings
When a Parsons auditor discovers a violation that may merit an expedited hearing, the auditor will contact the audit
manager and report the findings. Our audit manager will contact PennDOT via telephone and request an expedited
hearing. If PennDOT agrees, the audit report will be electronically transmitted to PennDOT, who will prepare the hearing
documents and send them to the regional office. The hearing examiner will schedule the hearing following PennDOT’s
time frames. Electronic document transfer speeds up the hearing process.
Immediate Hearings
When a Parsons auditor discovers a violation that may warrant an immediate suspension, the auditor will call the audit
manager and report the findings. The audit manager will contact PennDOT via email or telephone to provide details of
the violations and request an immediate hearing. If PennDOT agrees, the hearing can be held by telephone with the
auditor and station representative. If an immediate suspension is necessary, PennDOT can verbally order the auditor to
suspend the station or technician. PennDOT will also send w

end written documentation to the regional office for subsequent
delivery to the affected station or technician, and a hearing will be scheduled within three days of the suspension.
Hearing Procedures
The hearing examiner will hold the hearing as scheduled, obtain identification from all participants, and document it on
the electronic version of the MV-390 hearing abstract form. The hearing examiner will explain the hearing procedure
and record all testimony, including documentation of all evidence received. All participants will be advised that
PennDOT will make a decision based on all information presented. The hearing examiner will print the hearing abstract,
attach a copy of the hearing letter, and forward the electronic packet to PennDOT for review and appropriate action.
Penalties
At PennDOT’s direction, Parsons will take appropriate action regarding the I/M station and/or inspection personnel.
These actions can include the delivery of warnings, fines, and/or suspensions for I/M stations, inspectors, and repair
technicians. When PennDOT notifies Parsons of the hearing results, the hearing examiner will update the hearing
tracking system and provide a copy of the decision to th

2.3.1.1.4.M MAC Lanes (RFP Section 2.3.1.1.4.M)
As described in our response to Section 2.3.1.23, converting one lane at each the Inspection Program Station to support
enhanced MAC activities will allow for quick, seamless conversion of the lane to a full-service testing lane
should the demand arise during normal operating hours. We will not allow MAC equipment or operation to
interrupt safe, convenient, and efficient testing of vehicles presented for normal the Inspection Program tests.
Our solution for staffing MAC Lanes provides the best resources in the industry under an efficient, scalable
delivery system. Scalability will allow the MAC Lanes to accommodate higher public demand as the need for
more effective vehicle emissions repairs increases. This approach will improve the the Inspection Program’s effectiveness by
matching support resources with public demand for testing older vehicles as well as newer, increasingly
complex vehicles with more complex emissions failures.
